payload.description: Recovery doc docs/how-to/fix-fgos-write-rejected-merge-block.md's restore-paths-and-amend recipe is now impossible to execute on long-lived fgw/* branches forked before the events.jsonl log migration: merge.mjs's self-heal for stale-but-append-only-prefix .fgos/ drift only fires for paths tagged merge=union in .gitattributes, and that attribute was retired for events.jsonl by a recent unrelated change. Meanwhile .githooks/pre-commit's stagedFgosChangesOnWorkerBranch guard (tsk-5pb) now categorically refuses ANY .fgos/ change on ANY fgw/* branch commit in either direction, so the doc's own documented fix can no longer land. Discovered while recovering tsk-34o5 from repeated merge-conflict friction (workaround used instead: confirm the item's real commits never touch .fgos/, then git rebase main onto the item branch instead of merging, which drops the stale .fgos/ drift at the source). This will likely recur for the next long-lived branch that forked before the events.jsonl migration. Needs triage: either restore union-merge coverage for events.jsonl, or update the recovery doc's recipe to match the newer worker-branch write guard.

payload.title: Work items whose own verify field shells 'node --test ...' directly instead of through 'npm test'…
payload.description: Work items whose own verify field shells 'node --test ...' directly instead of through 'npm test' silently bypass the FGOS_DISABLE_OPPORTUNISTIC_CHECKS=1 env var that npm test's script wrapper carries (added by the already-delivered tsk-oet fix for opportunistic-check pollution). Confirmed live on tsk-67o (2026-08-24): its verify field ran node --test directly, causing spurious test failures that were only a false-negative from the missing env var, not a real regression -- fixed by editing the item's verify field to prefix FGOS_DISABLE_OPPORTUNISTIC_CHECKS=1. Any other open item whose verify field shells node --test directly (bypassing npm test) may hit the same spurious-failure class. Suggest a systemic fix: either a doctor check that flags verify fields calling node --test without that env var prefix, or documentation/convention enforcement at planning time so new items never write a bare node --test verify command.

payload.title: main-checkout.lock's wait/error messaging labels contention as 'likely your own session's other…
payload.description: main-checkout.lock's wait/error messaging labels contention as 'likely your own session's other in-flight call' whenever the holder pid string matches the caller's own environment-derived session identity -- but that identity is shared across ALL subagents/sub-sessions spawned under the same top-level Claude Code session, so the message is misleading whenever the real lock holder is actually a different SIBLING subagent (not the same in-flight call). Confirmed live 2026-08-24: while driving tsk-67o's approve retries, the lock was actually held by a concurrently-running sibling subagent (tsk-4dk-1's long retro-loop sweep, doing near-continuous main-checkout commits) but every wait/timeout message attributed it to 'your own session's other in-flight call', which sent debugging down the wrong path (suspected a self-contention bug in the retrying subagent's own Monitor/retry loop, which was a real secondary issue but not the primary cause) before the real holder was found by checking git log timestamps directly. Suggest: either the lock file record additional identifying info beyond the shared session pid (e.g. a per-subagent/per-tool-call token) so contention messaging can distinguish 'you, literally this call' from 'a sibling under the same session', or the message wording itself be softened to acknowledge the ambiguity ('same session identity, possibly a different concurrent call') instead of asserting it's the caller's own in-flight call.

payload.title: Out-of-process dispatch (src/runner/dispatch/cli.mjs's executeExecutorCli / dispatch.mjs execute)…
payload.description: Out-of-process dispatch (src/runner/dispatch/cli.mjs's executeExecutorCli / dispatch.mjs execute) resolves the worker's repoRoot from the calling session's process.cwd() at dispatch time, instead of an explicit, pinned path -- when multiple sibling Claude Code subagents run concurrently under the SAME orchestrating session (spawned without isolation:'worktree'), they share EnterWorktree/cwd state, and a background dispatch call can silently capture a DIFFERENT sibling's cwd if a cross-worktree cwd race lands at just the wrong moment. Confirmed live 2026-08-24: driving tsk-3ys and tsk-ri8 concurrently (both plain general-purpose subagents under one orchestrating session, no isolation:'worktree'), tsk-3ys's real out-of-process worker dispatch (node src/runner/dispatch.mjs execute fgos-coding-implement) produced a real, correct commit (512ee690, adding the '# Iron Law evidence' section to worker-prompt-skill-pointer.txt exactly per tsk-3ys's own plan.md) -- but the commit landed on fgw/tsk-ri8 instead of fgw/tsk-3ys, mislabeled with tsk-ri8's item id in the commit message. Caught only because the receiving driver (drive-tsk-ri8) independently verified its own dispatch result against real git state instead of trusting the worker's prose completion summary (the summary claimed a different, false commit sha that does not exist). Recovered non-destructively via git revert on the wrong branch (original commit still fully reachable by SHA) plus a cherry-pick onto the correct branch. This is a more severe manifestation of the already-known EnterWorktree cwd-sharing race (previously confirmed causing plain cwd drift and a stray npm run build:skills write into a sibling's worktree) -- here it silently misattributes REAL COMMITTED WORK to the wrong item's branch, which is much harder to catch (requires independently verifying commit SHAs/content, not just noticing an error). Suggested fix directions (not locked, for planning to size): (a) executeExecutorCli/dispatch.mjs execute should resolve and pass an explicit, already-validated repoRoot/worktree path at call time rather than reading process.cwd() lazily inside the dispatch call, closing the race window; (b) more broadly, concurrent same-session subagents driving different fgOS items should be a documented hard requirement to use isolation:'worktree' (or equivalent per-agent cwd isolation) at spawn time, not just a soft recommendation -- this incident happened specifically because that wasn't done.

payload.title: The .fgos store's lifecycle tracking (stage/status/decisions/discovery/gates) is losing/desyncing…
payload.description: The .fgos store's lifecycle tracking (stage/status/decisions/discovery/gates) is losing/desyncing data under concurrent write load, confirmed live 2026-08-24/25 across two separate incidents in the same session (multiple concurrent drivers doing approve/catchup/pick retries against the shared main checkout): (1) tsk-ri8 and tsk-3ys both had their ENTIRE session-long discovery/planning/decision/gate event history vanish from every .fgos/events/*.jsonl shard (checked all of them) mid-drive, reverting their live-read status/stage back to the original-submission placeholder (todo/discovery), while their real git branch commits (plan.md, implementation, Iron Law evidence) stayed fully intact -- this matches the already-researched gap in docs/history/events-jsonl-merge-abort-truncation-gap/RESEARCH.md (git merge --abort reverts the whole main-checkout tree to pre-abort HEAD, discarding any uncommitted events.jsonl tail appended concurrently by OTHER drivers' lifecycle writes, not just the aborting call's own) but that research's fix apparently has not landed or does not cover this trigger path. (2) A second, distinct desync: after tsk-ri8's fgos approve genuinely succeeded (git log confirms real merge commit 57e62de5 on main, JSON response confirmed to:'delivered'), fgos show tsk-ri8 still read back stage:discovery/status:todo -- while fgos list and fgos move (which correctly refused 'no transition from delivered to delivered') both agreed the item WAS actually delivered. This is a read-path inconsistency between fgos show and fgos list/move for the same item's same underlying state, distinct from the event-loss class (no data was actually lost this time -- the store had it right, but one read path reported it wrong). Both classes need investigation: the write-side event-loss (thread result.error/checkpoint more aggressively under concurrent load, or make merge --abort commit-then-revert instead of discarding uncommitted tail) and the read-side show-vs-list/move inconsistency (likely a caching or projection bug specific to the show verb).

payload.title: Out-of-process worker completion-signal detector reads a [DONE] token wrapped in markdown…
payload.description: Out-of-process worker completion-signal detector reads a [DONE] token wrapped in markdown backticks (`[DONE]`) as outcome:'unsignaled' (no signal) instead of a real completion -- confirmed live 2026-08-24/25 driving tsk-4e1: the out-of-process worker (agy/gemini-3.6-flash-medium) wrapped its own [DONE] token in backticks both times it reported completion, and real work had landed (verified independently via git log/git show, not the worker's own prose) both times, yet the mechanical detector reported unsignaled. This is the same class of gap tsk-5gd's fix already addressed, but in the OPPOSITE direction: tsk-5gd fixed a false-positive (a backtick-quoted [DONE] mentioned in passing being misread as a real signal); this is a false-negative (a genuine backtick-wrapped [DONE] token being misread as no-signal at all). Both are the same underlying issue -- the detector's token-matching needs to treat markdown-code-formatted [DONE] the same as a bare one, not as two different literal strings. Worth checking whether this executor/model (gemini-3.6-flash-medium via agy) has a habit of wrapping the completion token in backticks, and whether the detector's regex/match logic already handles this or needs an update.

payload.title: Bug: a blind '.fgos config sweep' commit can silently undo a deliberate, unrelated config edit…
payload.description: Bug: a blind '.fgos config sweep' commit can silently undo a deliberate, unrelated config edit sitting live in the same file. Concrete incident 2026-08-27: commit 21966be3c9bd945ac9cbec8e1b8d29823466ad7a (2026-08-26 21:05) deliberately reverted capabilities.fgos-coding-implement.prefer from the confirmed-broken agy-herdr (its -i interactiveMode invocation never delivers the prompt -- headBefore==headAfter, idle REPL banner, zero real work, confirmed twice) back to agy-cli, with an explicit 'do not flip back until fixed and re-verified live' note in the file's own description field. Commit 5d4891f632a4941d44fe062d28fa7ee4e0d84058 (2026-08-27 10:03, 'chore(.fgos): sweep dirty event shards on main checkout') then blindly git-added and committed whatever live .fgos/config.json state happened to be sitting on disk at sweep time -- silently flipping prefer BACK to agy-herdr, undoing the deliberate fix 13 hours later, with nobody intending that change and no mention of it in the sweep commit's own message (which only talks about event-log shards, never config.json's semantic content). Confirmed live a third time driving tsk-4o7: dispatch.mjs execute routed via=herdr-spawn per the clobbered prefer, and the out-of-process worker sat idle for the full 2100000ms timeout with zero real work (errorClass worker-timeout, clean tree afterward, no commit) -- exactly the failure mode 21966be3's own message predicted. Fixed live this round via commit 04465609335b256227ed9fec9c6f5478ab13efa0, restoring prefer to agy-cli. Root cause for follow-up: any 'sweep dirty state on main checkout' routine that blindly commits config.json (or any file carrying a deliberate, semantically-locked value like a capability prefer) without diffing against the last intentional value risks silently reverting a real bugfix. Needs either (a) excluding config.json's semantic fields from blind sweep commits, (b) a pre-commit diff check against the last deliberate value for known-sensitive config keys, or (c) some other mechanism -- open to whichever the next session's own discovery finds most honest, not locked here.
